summary.one_liner: Eclipse Mosquitto is an open source MQTT message broker (server) with C/C++ client libraries and command-line publish, subscribe and admin tools.
summary.what_it_does: Mosquitto implements an MQTT broker supporting protocol versions 5.0, 3.1.1 and 3.1. It ships a C and C++ client library plus the mosquitto_pub, mosquitto_sub and mosquitto_rr command-line utilities for publishing and subscribing. It also includes mosquitto_ctrl, mosquitto_signal and mosquitto_passwd for administering the broker. The broker is configured through a config file that defines listeners and authentication, and the README mentions an authentication methods section and a dynamic security plugin. Optional build features include TLS via OpenSSL, SQLite-based persistence, c-ares SRV lookup and an HTTP API via libmicrohttpd.
use_cases: Running a local MQTT broker for IoT or home automation messaging
Testing MQTT publish and subscribe from the command line
Building MQTT client applications with the C or C++ library
Securing a broker with listeners, authentication and TLS
how_to_run: On Windows and Mac: build with cmake; on other platforms: run make
make binary (to skip man page build when building from git)
notable: Full MQTT 5.0, 3.1.1 and 3.1 broker in one project
Includes client library plus pub/sub/admin command-line tools
Optional persistence, TLS, SRV lookup and HTTP API via build flags
Available as a vcpkg package on Windows, Mac and other platforms
Dynamic security plugin for managing access
caveats: Default startup allows anonymous access only from the local computer; a configuration file is needed for remote clients
Building from git sources requires xsltproc and docbook-xsl for man pages unless WITH_DOCS=no or make binary is used
Windows and Mac builds use cmake rather than plain make
